prompt.context: Our client is a provider of parking services in major metro areas around the United States. The CEO recently was driving to DTW airport and noticed a rise in private providers of parking. She thought to herself, should we enter this space? She has asked you to help her think about this and wants to brainstorm with you.
prompt.question: Should our client enter the airport parking market? Begin by assessing the attractiveness of this opportunity.

clarifying_info.a: Focus on O'Hare in Chicago, though you should recognize the ability to scale this to other airports.

clarifying_info.q: Where does our client currently operate?
clarifying_info.a: We are a US-based firm with parking lots located in cities — not at airports.

clarifying_info.q: What differences exist between urban parking and airport parking?
clarifying_info.a: The new service will have attendants, may need shuttle service, valet service, etc. Have the candidate brainstorm the differences.

clarifying_info.q: How many flights per day does O'Hare handle?
What is the average number of passengers per flight?
What percentage of fliers drive to the airport and need to park?
clarifying_info.a: 20% of fliers drive and need to park.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average parking stay?
What is the average price per day for parking?

framework: Market Size — estimate the size of the airport parking opportunity (O'Hare as proxy, scalable)
Competition — existing parking structures at the airport, other offsite parking providers, public transit alternatives (train, taxis, shuttles)
Existing Capability — differences between urban lots and airport lots (shuttle/busing system, customer service, valet, attendants)
Revenue — number of spaces sold, add-on services (car wash, newspaper), pricing strategies (frequent-park programs, packages)
Costs — land (rent or own), labor (bus drivers, ticket attendants, maintenance, security), insurance, promotion (coupons), fuel

questions.prompt: Estimate the market size for airport parking at O'Hare in Chicago.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build up from flights to passengers to parkers to parking days to revenue. Key steps: total annual passengers → divide by 2 (avoid double-counting arrivals and departures) → apply % who drive → multiply by average stay → multiply by daily rate. Strong candidates will note this can be scaled to other airports.

math.setup: Start with daily flights × passengers/flight × days/year to get total annual passengers. Divide by 2 to count only departing passengers (each trip = one departure + one arrival). Apply the share who drive and park, multiply by average stay length, then multiply by daily rate.
steps: Divide by 2 to avoid double-counting arriving/departing passengers = 37.5M unique traveler-trips
math.answer: ~$225M annual airport parking market at O'Hare

brainstorming.prompt: Brainstorm possible threats to the attractiveness of entering the airport parking market.

categories.name: Decline in airline travel demand
ideas: Higher fuel prices reducing air travel
Substitutes such as a high-speed rail network

categories.name: Alternative transportation to the airport
ideas: New or expanded public transit options
Improved ride-sharing services (e.g., Uber, Lyft) possibly enabled by social networking

categories.name: Competitive response
ideas: Number of existing competitors and their capacity to react
Price wars from established airport parking operators
Airport authority limiting or excluding new off-site providers

recommendation: There is approximately $225M of parking business at O'Hare, and this market is likely growing
Our existing knowledge of urban parking operations provides a foundation; this large opportunity could represent real growth
The opportunity appears worth exploring further before committing to full-scale entry
risks: Threats identified in brainstorming (demand decline, substitutes, ride-sharing growth)
Costs (land, shuttle operations, labor) could outweigh the revenue opportunity
Certain airport markets may already be oversaturated with competitors
next_steps: Carefully analyze the competitive landscape and unit economics at each target airport
Evaluate local competition and cost structures market by market
Determine if new transportation substitutes (ride-sharing, transit expansion) are in the pipeline
If proceeding, pilot at one airport before full-scale implementation
Leverage existing multi-city presence to scale efficiently across the portfolio
